label: late copy-phase steps whose input is one of d/z/2/u/s/f/p/n/w/b
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never during the original tokens or on <DEL>, and never on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=0 always, which follows from being in the copy phase). Its rate rises steeply with absolute step t: about 0 below t=8, 9% at t=11, 50% at t=17. So it fires mostly in long sequences (L=8-9 hold 81% of mass), at late recall positions near the end of the copy. On top of that it depends on the input token: d, z, 2, u, s and f fire most often (rates 13-18%), p/n/w/b fire moderately, and t and q rarely. The highest activations are on the last one or two copy steps of length-9 sequences, with inputs such as u, d, z, 2. On the dev split, the predicate (copy phase, t>=12, input in that set) gets P 0.65, R 0.67, F1 0.66 and mass recall 0.78. Copy phase plus recall_idx>=4 alone covers 91% of activations (94% of mass) but has precision 0.24. Misses include steps at t=8-11 and other input tokens (o, t, 0, k). The activation looks like a graded function of step and token identity, not a crisp rule.
